title: Multiplayer Normal Map Painting Tool on 3D Surface
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a multiplayer normal map painting tool on a 3D surface using Three.js. Requirements:

## Scene Setup
- Create a scene with a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 2, 5) looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.3) and a directional light at (5, 5, 5) with intensity 1.0.
- Place a subdivided plane geometry (64x64 segments, size 4x4) centered at origin, rotated to face the camera (-Math.PI/2 on X). Apply a MeshStandardMaterial with a dynamically generated normal map (512x512 canvas texture).
- Add a sphere (radius 0.3) at position (2, 1, 0) as a lighting reference object with MeshStandardMaterial metalness=0.5, roughness=0.3.
- Use OrbitControls for camera manipulation (disable during painting).

## Normal Map Painting System
- Implement raycasting on the plane to detect UV coordinates of mouse position.
- When painting mode is active and mouse is pressed, paint normal vectors onto the 512x512 canvas that serves as the normal map.
- Brush properties: size (5-50 pixels, default 15), strength (0.0-1.0, default 0.5), direction mode (raise/lower/left/right).
- 'Raise' mode paints normals pointing outward (RGB: 128, 128, 255 biased toward blue+strength).
- 'Lower' mode paints normals pointing inward (RGB: 128, 128, 0 biased away from blue).
- 'Left' mode biases red channel down, 'Right' mode biases red channel up.
- Each stroke must blend with existing normal map data using the strength parameter.

## Multiplayer Simulation
- Simulate 2 additional 'remote' players (Player B and Player C) with different colored cursor indicators on the 3D surface (green ring for B, blue ring for C).
- Every 2 seconds, Player B paints a small random stroke (5 pixels) at a random UV position in 'raise' mode.
- Every 3 seconds, Player C paints a small random stroke (8 pixels) at a random UV position in 'left' mode.
- Track total stroke count per player. Local user is Player A (red cursor ring).

## Undo/Redo System
- Maintain a history stack (max 20 entries) storing snapshots of the normal map canvas ImageData.
- Ctrl+Z triggers undo (restores previous state), Ctrl+Y triggers redo.
- Remote player strokes are also recorded in the history (but marked with player ID).
- Undo only undoes the local player's strokes (skips remote strokes in history).

## UI/HUD
- Top-left panel with: current brush size, strength, direction mode, active player count.
- Buttons: 'Raise', 'Lower', 'Left', 'Right' to switch direction mode.
- A slider for brush size and a slider for brush strength.
- Display stroke counters for all 3 players.
- A 'Clear Map' button that resets the normal map to flat (128, 128, 255) everywhere.
- A 'Toggle Paint Mode' button (default: ON). When OFF, OrbitControls work normally.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- paintMode: boolean (true when painting is active)
- brushSize: number (current brush size in pixels)
- brushStrength: number (0.0-1.0)
- directionMode: string ('raise'|'lower'|'left'|'right')
- strokeCountA: number (local player stroke count)
- strokeCountB: number (Player B stroke count)
- strokeCountC: number (Player C stroke count)
- historyLength: number (current history stack length)
- historyIndex: number (current position in history)
- canUndo: boolean
- canRedo: boolean
- lastPaintUV: {u: number, v: number} or null (last painted UV coordinate)
- normalMapPixel: {r: number, g: number, b: number} (sampled pixel at center 256,256)
- playerCursorsVisible: number (count of visible remote cursors)
- cameraDistance: number (distance from camera to origin)
- totalPixelsPainted: number (cumulative pixels modified by all players)
- isOrbiting: boolean (whether OrbitControls are active)
physics_constraints: Normal vectors must remain normalized (length ~1.0 when decoded from RGB). RGB values must stay in 0-255 range. Brush blending must be additive with clamping. History stack must not exceed 20 entries. Undo must only affect local player strokes. Remote player painting intervals must be consistent (2s and 3s respectively).
